title: Realtime Voice Agents with Frontier Intelligence — Bohan Li, EliseAI
talk_summary: Bohan Li describes a cascaded realtime voice harness (streaming speculative transcription, background tool-calling agents, prefix-cached TTS) built to hide latency while keeping frontier-model intelligence. The transferable core is speculative/eager execution with cancellation and background pre-fetching of tool results.

takeaways.technique: Background agents pre-execute tool calls into main agent context
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of the main (slow, expensive) agent doing tool-call round trips, background agents run the tool calls and push results into the main agent's context so it 'thinks it made the tool call, but it really didn't.'

Each partial transcription triggers an early agent generation that is only emitted once the user finishes speaking; if better context (corrected transcript, tool results) arrives, the eager generation is canceled and retriggered.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our eager kind of agent generation that was made without any tool calls is going to get canceled because the background agent finally is able to find

takeaways.technique: Prefix cache for repeated output segments
takeaways.what_they_do: Before synthesizing audio, they check whether a prefix of the agent's streamed text was already generated before and replay cached audio, only sending the cache-miss tail to the TTS provider.
A fast streaming transcriber runs continuously while a slower, more accurate batch model corrects it when it has more context; corrections override earlier output.
The accurate transcription layer uses the preceding question as context to fix ambiguous spans (e.g., recognizing a name vs. a date of birth) that the fast layer got wrong.
takeaways.evidence_quote: because the scribe V2 layer understands, you know, the the context of the question, it's able to understand that this is talking about name
